title: 2. Lok Sabha – House of the People

blocks.content: The Lok Sabha is the popular house of the Parliament and represents the people of India as a whole.

rows: Permanent body (1/3rd members retire every 2 years)
Limited powers (Can delay Money Bill by max 14 days)

items: The 104th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2019 discontinued the provision for nominating two Anglo-Indian members to the Lok Sabha.
A Motion of No-Confidence can only be introduced and passed in the Lok Sabha, not the Rajya Sabha.
In case of a joint sitting (Article 108), the Speaker of the Lok Sabha presides over the session.
The Rajya Sabha has only 14 days to return a Money Bill passed by the Lok Sabha, with or without recommendations.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Lok Sabha is the lower house of India's bicameral Parliament, directly elected by the people through universal adult suffrage.
The normal tenure of the Lok Sabha is five years from the date of its first meeting, though it can be dissolved earlier by the President.
To qualify for membership, a candidate must be a citizen of India and not less than 25 years of age.
Money Bills can only be introduced in the Lok Sabha and cannot be rejected or amended by the Rajya Sabha.
The Speaker is elected by the Lok Sabha from among its members to conduct the business of the House.
